question: How many hours per week can I work part-time?
required_facts: For Seoul, undergraduate, Korean standard met: 20 hours per week (25 at IEQAS-certified universities)
For Seoul, master's/doctoral, Korean standard met: 30 hours per week
For ERICA, bachelor's year 1-2, Korean level 3 met: 30 hours on weekdays, no restriction on weekends and school holidays
For ERICA, master's/doctoral, Korean level 4 met: 35 hours on weekdays, no restriction on weekends and school holidays
gold_evidence: The number of allowed hours for part-time work (For those submitting the Korean language proficiency standard) is 20 hours per week for language training students, 20 hours per week for undergraduate students (25 hours for IEQAS-certified universities), and 30 hours per week for masters/doctoral degree students. (https://oia.hanyang.ac.kr/notice/1813514) | Bachelor's | Year 1-2 | Level 3 | O | No Restrictions | 30 hours | No Restrictions (https://global.hanyang.ac.kr/eng/s3/s3_1.php) | Master's/Doctoral | N/A | Level 4 | O | No Restrictions | 35 hours | No Restrictions (https://global.hanyang.ac.kr/eng/s3/s3_1.php)
reply:
The number of allowed part-time work hours depends on your student status and Korean language proficiency level.

*   **Language training students:** 20 hours/week (if TOPIK Level 2); limited to 10 hours/week if the standard is not fulfilled [E1].
*   **Undergraduate students:** 20 hours/week (if TOPIK Level 3); limited to 10 hours/week if the standard is not fulfilled [E1].
    *   *Note:* If you are at an IEQAS-certified university, undergraduate students may work up to 25 hours/week [E1].
*   **Masters/Doctoral degree students:** 30 hours/week (if TOPIK Level 4 or higher); limited to 15 hours/week if the standard is not fulfilled [E1].
*   **Applicants with a research study visa (D-2-5):** Not permitted to work part-time unless they have received special permission for extension of stay due to thesis preparation. If granted such permission, they may work up to 30 hours/week [E2].

**Clarifying Question:** What is your current student status (e.g., undergraduate, master's, doctoral) and your TOPIK level?
